chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abd al-Malik al-Qummi, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abd al-Hamid (the servant of Isma'il ibn Ja'far), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"The prayer is completed (as qasr) in four places: in al-Masjid al-Haram, and the mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and the mosque of Kufa, and the shrine of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)."

key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الرَّسُولِ: The Mosque of the Messenger (in Medina)

ai.seo_question: What are the four places where prayer is completed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the four sacred precincts (*arba'at al-mawaṭin*) where the traveler’s prayer is considered complete (*tattimmu*), thereby exempting them from the usual shortening (*qasr*) rules. While the first two locations are universally recognized in Sunni and Shia jurisprudence, the inclusion of the Mosque of Kufa and the Shrine of Imam al-Husayn highlights the distinct Shia emphasis on the spiritual and legal sanctity of the Imams' shrines and key historical centers of authority. This ruling underscores the theological elevation of Karbala and Kufa as equivalent to the two holiest cities in terms of ritual status for pilgrims and travelers.
